title: Beyond the 956: Jay Rockefeller, former West Virginia governor and five-term U.S. senator, dies at 89
excerpt: Jay Rockefeller, the great-grandson of oil tycoon John D. Rockefeller who served two terms as governor of West Virginia and five terms in the U.S. Senate, has died at 89. He died on Friday, November 6, 2026, at his home in Washington, D.C. His family did not provide a cause of death.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Jay Rockefeller, the great-grandson of oil tycoon John D. Rockefeller who became governor of West Virginia and later a five-term U.S. senator, has died at 89.

Rockefeller died on Friday, November 6, 2026, at his home in Washington, D.C. His death was first reported by The Washington Post. His family did not provide a cause of death.

Born John Davison Rockefeller IV on June 18, 1937, in New York City, he was the great-grandson of Standard Oil founder John D. Rockefeller. He first came to West Virginia in 1964 as a VISTA volunteer, and the state became his lifelong home. He served in the West Virginia House of Delegates, as West Virginia secretary of state, and then as governor from 1977 to 1985.

In 1984, he was elected to the U.S. Senate, where he served five terms until his retirement in 2015. Over three decades in the Senate, he became known as a leading voice for expanding health care for the poor, helping to create the Children's Health Insurance Program, and he chaired the Senate Commerce Committee. He was also a vocal critic of the handling of the Iraq War.

Rockefeller is survived by his wife, Sharon Percy Rockefeller, and their children.

Rest in Peace, Jay Rockefeller.

Sources: The Washington Post, which first reported his death; Reuters; The Wall Street Journal.
